At present i have made goods of worth 25,000 rupees , but now customer says to cancel the order and refund the money. If i sell this goods in open market then there will be a loss around 10,000 rs , that is , i will get 15,000 (25,000 - 10,000= 15,000). In case i agree to cancel the order with customer, then can i keep his 10,000 rupees with me to compensate my loss, and refund him 5,000 (15,000 - 10,000=5000) ?. Please reply in detail and along with proof . 1725 views Q. After retirement I invested my PF amount in a business looked after by my sister-in-law in Australia. She deals with properties and owns many properties and Estates and get rent from them. She must have taken bank loans to purchase the properties and must have paid bank interest also. She suggested to me to invest my amount in her business and she would give me 14% profit for the first year. Each year the profit percentage changes. For last year I got about 18% profit. It is also agreed that if she incur losses, the losses will be shared by me also. Further she said after deducting all the maintenance expenses etc., the profit will be calculated each year. It was also agreed that whenever I want I can discontinue the business with her and I will get back my whole invested amount. Could you tell me with the above conditions the profit what I am getting is Halal ? Suppose I discontinue the business with her and if I get back my whole amount, should I pay the Zakath for the previous years when the amount was in her possession or should I pay the Zakath once the amount come to me and remain with me for one full year? Right now I pay the Zakath for the profit amount which remains with me unused/surplus for one year. 1595 views Q. answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Business Question ID: 41596 Country: India Title: Selling Clothes of Women Question: I am planning to start a business selling modern BURQA (niqab) which has designs, colours and lots of stones on that. Is it lawful to sell these kinds of burqas according to Islam which is more attractive than the normal type of burqas with no designs or any stones on that? Since it is more attractive than normal burqas few people suggest me that it is haram to do business with these. Please clarify. Answer ID: 41596 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1585/1193/D=1433) When a woman wears any cloth or jewellery then it also carried the same ruling which body of a woman has. So as a woman is asked to cover her body parts in the same way all the things related to adornments on her body should also be covered. Thus big chuddar or simple burqah is only so that her adornments (clothes etc) are covered. Had the body clothes been enough to cover the body parts then why this Quranic commandment was given? يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِن جَلَابِيبِهِنَّ . O prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers that they should draw down their shawls over them. It is so that the face and the things of adornment (clothes and jewellery etc) are covered with it. It is obvious that the expediency of the order of the Quran and Hadith i.e. the Hijab shall be gained with simple and big chuddar. If the burqah is also adorned and embroidered then it shall resemble the clothes of adornment for women then it shall also be required to be covered with hijab. In this case it shall be wrong to say it burqah rather it shall be an adorned cloth for which it shall be wajib to cover it. With the said details, the reply of your question was clear that it shall be a sin to say it burqah and it shall be promotion of fashion against Islamic interest which shall cause another sin. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
